newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open firmer in wake of U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open firmer in wake of U.S. data.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened stronger in active trade on Friday amid weaker-than-expected U.S. employment data and further gains in the Canadian dollar, dealers said.
"We saw the market rallying after the number, and now we're seeing some profit-taking. I don't really know where we're going to settle out," said a T-bill trader with one bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.07 percent from 3.13 percent at the close of trading on Thursday.

Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets rallied after the U.S. Labor Department reported the economy added 142,000 new jobs in April, below expectations of a 211,000 increase. However, the report also showed the jobless rate fell to 4.9 percent, the lowest in over 23 years.

Canada's dollar also rallied following the data, providing further support for the money market. The currency rallied past C$1.3825 (US$0.7233) as investors continued to bet against the possibility of a U.S. Federal Reserve rate hike on May 20, analysts said.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.49 percent from 3.51 percent at Thursday's close. The one-year T-bill firmed to yield 4.04 percent from 4.07 percent on Thursday.
The call loan rate traded at 3.0 percent, in the center of the Bank of Canada's 2.75-3.25 percent target range.
